MAGNO Dear Mr. Magno ThlS has reference to your email dated April 3, 2025, requesting the Department 3 legal opinion on whether or not it is legal for a private institution more particularly a cooperatve to hold office in the barangay hall. At the outset, barangay halls serve as the official seat of the smallest unit of local govemment. It functions as a vital hub for governance, community service, and public admuntstration. It is where the barangay council holds its sessions, residents access basc services, and a place where various programs such as health and social welfare are beng coordinated. As a government funded facility, the barangay hall IS intended to be accessible space for all constituents, ensuring that government services are delrvered effectively and that the community needs are addressed in an inclusive and ransparent manner. Section 4 (2) of Presidential Decree No. 1445 governs the use of government property lay.ng he basic guidelines in the use thereof— Financial transactions and Section 4. Fundamental principles — operations of any govemment agency shall be govemed by the fundamental principles set forth hereunder, to wit: (2) Govemment funds or property shall be spent or used solely for public purposes In addressing your aforementioned query, this level is of the considered view that the utilization of the barangay hall as an office for the cooperative or for business-related activities constitutes a breach of its designated purpose, given that it IS fundamentally established for governmental functions, serving as the seat of local governance and a venue for community meetjngs and activities. Moreover, Section 4 of RA 67131 mandates that, xxx [a]ll govemment resources and powers ot their respective offices must be employed and used efficiently, effectively honestly and economically, particularly to avoid wastage in public funds anci revenues. The mandate stated above underscores the obligation of public officials to manage government properties and facilities Including barangay halls With utmost integrity and accountability Allowing a private entity such as cooperatives to use public infrastructure rent-free, while also benefitting trom its utilities at no cost. contradicts "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" No 3454

this principle. It constitutes a form of indirect subsidy using public resources, which, if not sanctioned by law or justifies by a clear public interest, may be deemed as a misuse of government property and a violation of the public trust. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have provided you sufficient guidance on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LLRALD/mag page 2 Of 2
